Hi Avery,

We have a candidate, Daniel Park, for Req 3245 (Senior Platform Engineer). Recruiting and Total Rewards ran the comp simulation and recommend the following standard offer for sign-off:

- Base: $210,000
- Bonus (target): 15% annual (non-guaranteed)
- Equity: 0.25% (4-year vest, 1y cliff) broken into: 0.10% immediate hire tranche + 0.15% performance tranche (year 2-4)
- Start date: target Jan 18, 2027

Rationale: candidate has strong infra background, several competing offers; paymix skews slightly to cash (base + sign-on) to meet team budget while preserving upside via a small performance-tranche RSU to stay within band.

Attachments: req3245-offer-summary.pdf (PDF), equity-tranche-model.xlsx (XLSX)

Two items we want you to confirm:
1) Approve the recommended paymix above, or request a shift (e.g., increase equity to 0.4% and reduce base by $15k).
2) If approved, confirm sign-on authority (recruiting is requesting a one-time sign-on of $25k to match counteroffer).

If you'd like a quick call, I can jump on now. If not, a reply with your preferred option is great — we need decision by EOD Monday to keep timeline.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Compensation & Talent @ Redwood Inference

Avery, Laura —

Quick answers and a short downside scenario below. See updated equity-tranche-model.xlsx for the cash/equity permutations.

1) Immediate tranche mechanics: the 0.10% is a standard RSU grant that vests on the regular 4-year schedule (1y cliff). It is not accelerated at hire; the intent is retention through the first year. The performance tranche (0.15%) vests on milestones tied to on-call participation and project delivery (documented in the hire memo).

2) Sign-on structure: recommendation is $10k cash + $15k in RSU top-up (time-vested, 2-year straight-line) to balance upfront competitiveness and ongoing retention. Tax treatment: cash is regular payroll. RSU top-up follows standard taxation at vest.

3) Downside scenario if candidate pushes for 0.4% equity:
- Option A (approve 0.4%): increases comp spend in year 1 by ~$45k TCO (equity accrual + comp). Approve only if team budget has reserve or is willing to reallocate from non-critical hires.
- Option B (counter with $30k sign-on + 0.25% equity): more cash upfront, slight increase in immediate cost but keeps long-term equity dilution lower.
- Option C (hold to original): risk of losing candidate to stronger equity offer. Recruiting estimates 30% chance candidate will decline if we don't sweeten equity.

Recommendation: Approve original structure with the $10k/$15k split sign-on — preserves band discipline and gives recruiting a reasonable counter. If you want to prioritize retention over band, approve 0.4% and we'll route for headcount/finance reallocation.

Attachments: updated equity-tranche-model.xlsx

Karthik
